comments.body: Hi @positive666, do you mind picking up this PR again? I will help you review and get it merged. I think there are new changes that the PR requires additional adaptation. Also, I think `_can_use_fused_gdn_nonspec_decode` can be simplified a bit.

Thanks @gau-nernst, updated in `09fcbef970`. Adapted to the current GDN interfaces and simplified the non-spec guard. The CUDA 12.9 extension build and all 125 GPU tests passed on L20.

Updated performance and GSM8K results, including limitations

Thank you @positive666, I didn't notice you updated your comment and results. I also ran some testing on GB300 with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next

conc | P50 TPOT base→head | Δ | P99 TPOT Δ | P50 TTFT Δ | out tok/s Δ
-- | -- | -- | -- | -- | --
1 | 4.53 → 4.55 ms | +0.45% | +0.96% | −5.6% (155.5→146.9) | −0.32%
4 | 6.36 → 6.08 ms | −4.35% | −4.41% | −4.6% | +4.52%
16 | 10.15 → 9.78 ms | −3.63% | −4.05% | −4.7% | +3.46%
64 | 19.87 → 19.44 ms | −2.18% | −2.25% | −9.7% (673.5→608.4) | +2.29%

Good improvement for c=4-64, though it's surprising that c=1 doesn't help much (we would expect c=1 has the most benefits). So I did a microbenchmark (gate computation + QK norm + GDN decode + gated output norm)

B | rec+norm (Triton) | fused op | path Δ
-- | -- | -- | --
1 | 5.41 | 5.74 | +0.37 (noise)
4 | 6.27 | 5.95 | -0.37
8 | 6.93 | 6.06 | -1.00
16 | 7.99 | 7.67 | -0.25
32 | 13.14 | 9.73 | -3.48
64 | 18.94 | 16.88 | -2.04
128 | 37.82 | 35.84 | -0.60
256 | 70.85 | 71.07 | +2.74 (fused loses)

Indeed the fused op is only better in medium range of M. Then I remembered about FlashInfer, so I also microbenchmark it

B | tri rec+norm | fus op | fi rec+norm | best
-- | -- | -- | -- | --
1 | 5.82 | 5.70 | 4.47 | fi
4 | 6.32 | 5.95 | 4.91 | fi
8 | 7.01 | 6.06 | 5.55 | fi
16 | 7.99 | 7.67 | 7.22 | fi
32 | 13.16 | 9.71 | 10.48 | fus
64 | 19.40 | 17.07 | 17.12 | fus
128 | 38.57 | 35.85 | 35.60 | fi
256 | 70.82 | 71.06 | 68.96 | fi

Given this result, I think we should prefer FlashInfer integration rather than trying to get this PR merge. What do you think?

@vadiklyutiy will you continue working on #41966? If not, either I or @positive666 (if you want) can take over.

Thanks @gau-nernst. Agreed on prioritizing FlashInfer. I'm happy to help with #41966 if @vadiklyutiy isn't continuing. I'll mark this PR as draft for now. Should we retain this CUDA path for L20/SM89?

@positive666 Can you do microbenchmark comparing Triton unfused vs CUDA fused vs FlashInfer unfused like I did above? I haven't checked if FlashInfer GDN decode supports L20/SM89. The microbenchmark results will show if it's worth to do fused CUDA for SM89.
OK, I’ll update you once I have the results. @gau-nernst

Hi, @gau-nernst  Completed the L20/SM89 three-way comparison with real Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 inputs, independent repeats, and 512-step replay. Timings below are microseconds (lower is better):

| dtype | B | cache | Triton | CUDA fused | FlashInfer |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| FP32 | 1 | warm | 6.34 | 5.87 | 4.81 |
| FP32 | 1 | cold | 12.14 | 10.24 | 10.45 |
| FP32 | 8 | warm | 19.15 | 18.19 | 17.10 |
| FP32 | 8 | cold | 74.26 | 76.63 | 74.96 |
| BF16 | 1 | warm | 4.23 | 5.08 | 4.02 |
| BF16 | 1 | cold | 7.82 | 7.12 | 7.16 |
| BF16 | 8 | warm | 11.92 | 14.16 | 15.88 |
| BF16 | 8 | cold | 35.74 | 37.19 | 39.14 |

FP32 replay passed for all six trajectories. BF16 outputs passed, but CUDA and FlashInfer both show sparse state-tolerance differences on the longest traces, consistent with accumulated numerical differences across backends.

The CUDA advantage is therefore limited to a narrow FP32 B=1 cold-state case (~2% over FlashInfer); it does not justify broad default dispatch. Since #41966 already covers the FlashInfer integration, I propose closing #53463 as superseded unless maintainers want to retain this CUDA path as an explicit SM89 opt-in.

This pull request has merge conflicts that must be resolved before it can be
merged. Please rebase the PR, @positive666.

https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/syncing-a-fork

@positive666 Vadim doesn't have bandwidth to work on FlashInfer kernel integration now, you can take over the work and open a new PR. As usual, please report microbenchmark and e2e perf improvements. If the FlashInfer kernel is always better, we can make it the default for `auto` too.

assessment: Reviewer-invited successor to open Draft #41966; current CustomOp/config, FP32-only pooled remapping, mixed decode and graph/cache-group integration differ materially. No additional successor found in issue context or open searches. #53645 is separate SM120 whole-layer decode; #60050/#60105 are prefill.
